summary: Emil Kowalski's mobile-native skill is an instruction file for an AI agent that makes a web app feel installed on a phone instead of like a website in a browser. It works from a symptom table of eleven common tells (sticky hover, the gray tap flash, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, pull-to-refresh hijacking scroll, content stopping at the notch, long-press selecting button text, carousels scrolling the wrong way, a mismatched status bar, and bugs that only show on real phones), and gives the reason and the exact CSS or meta tag for each. It insists on capability media queries instead of device sniffing, never disabling zoom, and testing on real hardware because device emulation reproduces none of these bugs. It ends with a baseline to ship before the first component and a 'Never Ship' self-check table. For a design system it supplies platform-layer defaults (viewport meta, hover gating, press feedback timing, input font size, safe-area padding, per-scheme theme-color) that every web component inherits.
key_ideas: Most 'feels janky on mobile' reports are platform-layer problems, not animation problems: a tap delay, a tap flash or a hover state that sticks.
The user's real phone is the source of truth; Chrome device emulation reproduces none of these bugs.
Almost every fix is one CSS declaration or one meta tag, so reaching for JavaScript is the wrong tool.
Gate by capability with media queries such as (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), never by user agent or screen width, because touch and mouse coexist on many devices.
Every fix carries its reason and is applied only where that reason holds; user-select: none is right on a button and a defect on body text.
Never disable zoom; the page zooms into inputs because their font size is under 16px, so fix the font size.
Press feedback must happen when the finger lands (:active or pointerdown), not on click, and it lasts 100-160ms with ease-out.
Use 100dvh for app shells and 100svh for heroes; 100vh overflows by the height of the URL bar.
Stop overscroll with overscroll-behavior (none on the root, contain on inner scrollers), never with a touchmove listener.
Paint edge to edge with viewport-fit=cover and pad content back with env(safe-area-inset-*).
touch-action names what the browser may still do: pan-y on a horizontal carousel, pan-x on a vertical sheet handle, none only on surfaces that own every axis.
Give each color scheme its own theme-color, matched to the header background at the top of the page, not the brand color.
A small baseline of meta tags and CSS should ship before the first component of any mobile-facing app.
When a fix cannot be verified without a device, say so instead of claiming it is fixed.

topics.name: Mobile app patterns
topics.summary: The whole source: eleven platform-layer fixes and a baseline that make a web app feel native on a phone, plus the rule to test on real hardware.

topics.name: Web implementation (CSS and React)
topics.summary: Exact CSS and meta tags: hover gating media query, tap highlight, dvh/svh, 16px inputs, touch-action, overscroll-behavior, viewport-fit=cover with env() insets, user-select, theme-color per scheme, and Tailwind and Next.js specifics.

topics.name: Accessibility
topics.summary: Never disable zoom with user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1; keep content text selectable; keep press feedback for touch users after removing the tap highlight.

topics.name: Micro-interactions
topics.summary: Press feedback fires on pointer-down via :active, uses scale(0.97) and a background change over 100ms, and stays within 100-160ms with ease-out.

topics.name: Easing and timing
topics.summary: Press feedback timing is 100-160ms with ease-out, reusing the animate skill's tokens instead of a new curve.

topics.name: Gestures and drag
topics.summary: touch-action tells the browser which axes an element owns (pan-y, pan-x, none, manipulation); native scroll-snap beats a hand-rolled spring for carousels.

topics.name: Drawers and sheets
topics.summary: Sheet content uses overscroll-behavior: contain, sheets pad the bottom with calc(1rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)), drag-to-dismiss surfaces use touch-action: none, and a vertical sheet handle uses pan-x.

topics.name: Forms and inputs
topics.summary: Inputs need a 16px minimum font size to stop iOS zoom, and the right inputmode, type, autocapitalize, autocorrect and enterkeyhint to set the keyboard.

topics.name: Buttons and actions
topics.summary: Buttons get touch-action: manipulation, user-select: none, an :active press state, and hover styles only behind a capability media query.

topics.name: Dark mode and themes
topics.summary: theme-color is set once per prefers-color-scheme, matched to the header background, and updated from JavaScript when the theme switches by class.

topics.name: Spacing and layout
topics.summary: Full-height layouts use 100dvh (app shell) or 100svh (hero), and fixed headers, bottom bars, toasts and sheets pad with safe-area insets.

topics.name: Design process
topics.summary: Match the symptom, apply the fix only where its reason applies, ship the baseline first, test on an older real phone with the keyboard open and in landscape, and report what still needs a device.

rules.rule: Ship every mobile fix with its reason, and apply it only where that reason applies, not globally out of habit.
rules.why: The same declaration can be correct in one place and a defect in another: user-select: none on body text is a defect, on a button it is correct.
rules.evidence: Hard Rules 1: Every fix ships with the reason

rules.rule: Detect capabilities with media queries and platform features ((hover: hover), (pointer: fine), env(), dvh); never branch on user agent strings or screen width to guess at touch.
rules.why: The platform tells you what it can do; guessing from device identity or width is wrong.
rules.evidence: Hard Rules 2: Media queries over device sniffing

rules.rule: Write interaction styles for touch and mouse at the same time and gate them by capability, not by device.
rules.why: Touch and mouse are not exclusive: iPads with trackpads, laptops with touchscreens, phones with a mouse.
rules.evidence: Hard Rules 3: Touch and mouse are not exclusive

rules.rule: Never disable zoom with user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1; fix the input font size that causes the zoom instead.
rules.why: Disabling zoom is an accessibility failure, and the real cause is inputs under 16px.
rules.evidence: Hard Rules 4: Never disable zoom

rules.rule: Test on real hardware before calling a mobile fix done: connect the phone, open the dev server by IP, and debug with Safari's Web Inspector or Chrome remote debugging.
rules.why: Emulation cannot reproduce sticky hover, tap delay, rubber-banding, safe areas, or the keyboard.
rules.evidence: Hard Rules 5: Test on hardware before calling it done

rules.rule: Never declare a mobile issue fixed based on Chrome device emulation.
rules.why: None of these bugs reproduce in device emulation; testing only there ships all of them.
rules.evidence: Never Ship: Declaring it fixed from device emulation; Operating Posture failure mode 1

rules.rule: Do not reach for JavaScript when CSS or a meta tag does the job; for example, hide hover states with a media query, not a useIsTouchDevice() hook.
rules.why: Almost every item is one declaration; JavaScript is the wrong tool.
rules.evidence: Reaching for JavaScript when CSS or a meta tag does it

rules.rule: When you cannot run the app on hardware, state which fixes you verified from code and which the user must confirm on a real device; never claim a device-only fix is fixed.
rules.why: The phone is the source of truth, and the honest answer is sometimes 'I can't verify this without a device'.
rules.evidence: Operating Posture; Tone

rules.rule: Put every :hover style inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
rules.why: Touch browsers fake hover on the first tap and leave it applied, so a button that scales up on hover stays scaled up after being tapped.
rules.evidence: 1. Hover state stuck after tap

rules.rule: Use both conditions in the hover gate, (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), not just one.
rules.why: (hover: hover) means the primary input can hover; (pointer: fine) means it is precise like a mouse and rules out styluses and the odd Android device that claims hover support.
rules.evidence: 1. Hover state stuck after tap: Both conditions matter

rules.rule: In Tailwind v4 rely on the hover: variant, which already compiles to @media (hover: hover); in Tailwind v3 set future.hoverOnlyWhenSupported.
rules.why: It gates hover by capability at the framework level.
rules.evidence: 1. Hover state stuck after tap

rules.rule: Give touch users press feedback through :active on every tappable element.
rules.why: :active works on every input type, and touch users still need feedback once hover is gated off.
rules.evidence: 1. Hover state stuck after tap: Touch users still need press feedback

rules.rule: Remove the tap highlight once, globally, with html { -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; }.
rules.why: The translucent flash on tap is the single loudest 'this is a website' signal and fights the press feedback you designed.
rules.evidence: 2. Gray/blue flash on tap

rules.rule: After removing the tap highlight, make sure every tappable element has its own :active state.
rules.why: You have removed the only feedback the browser was giving.
rules.evidence: 2. Gray/blue flash on tap

rules.rule: Use height: 100dvh, not 100vh, for app shells, drawers and anything bottom-pinned that should track the visible area as browser chrome shows and hides.
rules.why: 100vh is the largest viewport, so it overflows by the URL bar's height and a bottom-pinned button sits under the bar.
rules.evidence: 3. Layout has the wrong height; Never Ship: 100vh for an app shell or bottom-pinned UI

rules.rule: Use min-height: 100svh, not 100dvh, for marketing heroes and first screens.
rules.why: svh is the smallest the viewport gets, so nothing is cut off, and it is stable; dvh causes layout shifts on marketing content mid-scroll.
rules.evidence: 3. Layout has the wrong height; Never Ship: 100dvh on a marketing hero

rules.rule: Avoid lvh for layout heights.
rules.why: lvh is the old vh, the largest viewport; you almost never want it.
rules.evidence: 3. Layout has the wrong height

rules.rule: Add a 100vh fallback line above the dvh/svh declaration only if the project's support matrix demands old browsers.
rules.why: The fallback exists only for old browsers.
rules.evidence: 3. Layout has the wrong height

rules.rule: Set input, textarea and select font-size to 16px at the minimum.
rules.why: iOS Safari zooms the page on focus when the input font size is under 16px and does not zoom back out on blur, leaving a cropped, drifted layout.
rules.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input

rules.rule: If the design wants smaller input text on desktop, apply the 16px input size only under @media (pointer: coarse).
rules.why: It keeps the zoom fix where it matters without changing desktop input text.
rules.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input

rules.rule: Set inputmode="numeric" on code fields and inputmode="decimal" on amount fields.
rules.why: It sets the right software keyboard for the field.
rules.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input: set the keyboard

rules.rule: Use type="email" and type="tel" for email and phone fields.
rules.why: It sets the right software keyboard for the field.
rules.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input: set the keyboard

rules.rule: Set autocapitalize="none" and autocorrect="off" on username and code fields.
rules.why: The source lists it under setting the keyboard for the field; that auto-capitalisation and autocorrect would alter usernames and codes is [inferred].
rules.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input: set the keyboard

rules.rule: Set enterkeyhint ("send", "search" or "done") so the return key says what it does.
rules.why: The return key should describe its action.
rules.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input: set the keyboard

rules.rule: Apply touch-action: manipulation to button, a, [role="button"] and other tappable elements.
rules.why: Browsers wait 300ms after a tap to see whether a second tap (double-tap zoom) is coming; modern browsers skip the wait with width=device-width, but iOS Safari still delays on some elements; manipulation says the element never double-tap-zooms, so click fires immediately.
rules.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy: The 300ms click delay

rules.rule: Give press feedback on press, not release: style :active, and if JavaScript is needed listen to pointerdown, not click.
rules.why: Native buttons respond the instant the finger lands; feedback on click arrives when the finger leaves and reads as lag even at 0ms.
rules.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy: Feedback on release instead of press; Never Ship: Press feedback on click only

rules.rule: For button press feedback, transition transform and background over 100ms with ease-out, and on :active scale to 0.97 and change the background to var(--gray-4).
rules.why: It gives an immediate, native-feeling response when the finger lands.
rules.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy: .button:active code

rules.rule: Keep press feedback between 100 and 160ms with ease-out.
rules.why: The section's reason is that native buttons respond the instant the finger lands; the source gives no separate reason for the 100–160ms range. [inferred]
rules.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy: Keep press feedback at 100–160ms

rules.rule: If the codebase uses the animate skill's tokens, use them for press feedback; do not fork a new curve.
rules.why: The source gives no reason; keeping one set of curves consistent across the codebase is [inferred].
rules.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy: don't fork a new curve

rules.rule: In apps with their own scroll containers, drag-down drawers or a canvas, set overscroll-behavior: none on html and body.
rules.why: Scrolling past the top triggers pull-to-refresh on Android Chrome and the whole-page rubber band on iOS, which is wrong in an app.
rules.evidence: 6. Pull-to-refresh hijacks scroll

rules.rule: Keep pull-to-refresh (drop overscroll-behavior: none from html) when the app is a scrolling document where pull-to-refresh is welcome.
rules.why: Page-level overscroll is fine on a document.
rules.evidence: Drop `overscroll-behavior: none` from `html` if the app is a scrolling document where pull-to-refresh is welcome

rules.rule: On every inner scrollable (sheet content, chat list, sidebar) set overflow-y: auto and overscroll-behavior: contain; use none on the root and contain on children.
rules.why: contain keeps the container's own native-feeling bounce but stops scroll from chaining to the page behind it.
rules.evidence: 6. Pull-to-refresh hijacks scroll: .sheet-content

rules.rule: Never stop overscroll with a touchmove listener that calls preventDefault(); use overscroll-behavior.
rules.why: It blocks scrolling entirely and makes the listener non-passive, which costs frames.
rules.evidence: 6. Pull-to-refresh hijacks scroll; Never Ship

rules.rule: Add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta tag so the page paints edge to edge under the notch.
rules.why: By default the browser letterboxes the page inside the safe area, leaving notch, Dynamic Island and home-indicator zones in the body background; native apps paint edge to edge.
rules.evidence: 7. Content stops at the notch

rules.rule: Pad fixed headers, bottom tab bars, toasts and sheets with env(safe-area-inset-*): header padding-top env(safe-area-inset-top), bottom bar padding-bottom env(safe-area-inset-bottom), sheet padding-bottom calc(1rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)).
rules.why: Native apps pad their content away from the notch and home indicator; normal page content usually gets it for free through the header's padding.
rules.evidence: 7. Content stops at the notch

rules.rule: Never use env(safe-area-inset-*) without viewport-fit=cover in the viewport meta tag.
rules.why: Without the meta tag every env() safe-area value is 0px.
rules.evidence: 7. Content stops at the notch; Never Ship

rules.rule: Give env() a fallback, such as env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px), when the value is used inside calc().
rules.why: The calc needs a defined value where the inset is unavailable. [inferred]
rules.evidence: 7. Content stops at the notch: Give env() a fallback

rules.rule: Make control text unselectable: on button, [role="button"], .tab, .chip and .drag-handle set user-select: none, -webkit-user-select: none and -webkit-touch-callout: none.
rules.why: Long-press on a web button selects its label or pops the copy/share callout, which native controls never do; Safari still needs the -webkit- prefix.
rules.evidence: 8. Long-press selects button text

rules.rule: Never put user-select: none on body; apply it only to controls.
rules.why: Text that is content must stay selectable: users copy addresses, error messages and order numbers.
rules.evidence: 8. Long-press selects button text; Never Ship

rules.rule: On a horizontal JS-gesture carousel set touch-action: pan-y.
rules.why: A horizontal swipe is ambiguous to the browser, which often jitters the page up while the carousel moves; pan-y keeps vertical panning with the browser and gives horizontal to the carousel.
rules.evidence: 9. Carousel scrolls vertically

rules.rule: Use touch-action: none only on a surface whose custom gesture owns every axis, such as a drag-to-dismiss sheet or a slider.
rules.why: none means the element handles everything; elsewhere the user cannot scroll past it.
rules.evidence: 9. Carousel scrolls vertically: .drag-surface

rules.rule: On a vertical sheet handle set touch-action: pan-x.
rules.why: The sheet handles vertical drags; horizontal stays with the browser.
rules.evidence: 9. Carousel scrolls vertically: .vertical-sheet-handle

rules.rule: Choose a touch-action value by naming what the browser may still do, not what the element handles: pan-y on a horizontal carousel, pan-x on a vertical sheet handle.
rules.why: The values name what the browser may still do; pan-y on a horizontal carousel means the browser keeps vertical panning while the element handles horizontal.
rules.evidence: 9. Carousel scrolls vertically: The values name what the browser may still do

rules.rule: Never put touch-action: none on something the user needs to scroll past; use pan-x or pan-y.
rules.why: The user will not be able to scroll past it.
rules.evidence: on something the user needs to scroll past

rules.rule: If the carousel is native scroll rather than a JS gesture, prefer scroll-snap-type: x mandatory on the track and scroll-snap-align: start on slides.
rules.why: The browser's own physics beat a hand-rolled spring, and touch-action becomes unnecessary.
rules.evidence: If the carousel is native scroll rather than a JS gesture, prefer

rules.rule: Set one theme-color meta tag per prefers-color-scheme, plus <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">.
rules.why: The status bar and browser chrome take their color from theme-color; one value gives light mode a dark bar or dark mode a white one.
rules.evidence: 10. Status bar color doesn't match; Never Ship: One theme-color for both schemes

rules.rule: Match theme-color to the color at the very top of the page (the header background), not the brand color.
rules.why: The source gives no reason; that the status bar should blend into the top of the page is [inferred].
rules.evidence: 10. Status bar color doesn't match: Match the value to the color at the very top

rules.rule: In Next.js set theme-color through the viewport export with themeColor: [{ media, color }].
rules.why: That is where Next.js sets the tag.
rules.evidence: 10. Status bar color doesn't match: In Next.js

rules.rule: If the app switches theme with a class rather than the OS setting, update the theme-color tag from JavaScript on toggle.
rules.why: The per-scheme tags use prefers-color-scheme, which follows only the OS setting. [inferred]
rules.evidence: If the app switches theme with a class rather than the OS setting, update the tag from JavaScript on toggle

rules.rule: For an installed PWA, set apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style and the manifest's theme_color and background_color as the same decision as theme-color.
rules.why: They are the same decision for the status bar and chrome.
rules.evidence: For an installed PWA, `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` and the manifest's `theme_color`/`background_color` are the same decision

rules.rule: To test on a phone, connect it over USB, run the dev server on 0.0.0.0 and open it by the machine's LAN IP; debug iOS via Safari > Develop > the device and Android via chrome://inspect.
rules.why: Sticky hover, tap highlight, vh and the URL bar, input zoom, click delay, overscroll, safe areas and the software keyboard are all real-hardware behaviors.
rules.evidence: 11. Right in Chrome, wrong on phone

rules.rule: Test on a phone that is a few years old, not the newest one on your desk.
rules.why: Real users are not all on the newest device. [inferred]
rules.evidence: 11. Right in Chrome, wrong on phone

rules.rule: Test with the software keyboard open, and test in landscape at least once.
rules.why: The software keyboard is a real-hardware behavior that emulation misses; the source gives no separate reason for landscape.
rules.evidence: 11. Right in Chrome, wrong on phone

rules.rule: If installation is a target, test as an installed PWA.
rules.why: Standalone mode changes viewport, safe areas and status bar behavior.
rules.evidence: 11. Right in Chrome, wrong on phone

rules.rule: Do not treat the Xcode Simulator as the final check; real hardware is the bar.
rules.why: The Simulator is a step up from emulation but still misses touch feel.
rules.evidence: The Xcode Simulator is a step up from emulation but still misses touch feel

rules.rule: Ship the mobile baseline before the first component of any mobile-facing app.
rules.why: It is the floor for feeling native on mobile.
rules.evidence: Baseline: this is the floor. Ship it before the first component

rules.rule: Use the baseline viewport meta: width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content.
rules.why: interactive-widget=resizes-content makes the software keyboard shrink the layout viewport on Android Chrome, so 100dvh and bottom-pinned inputs react as they do on iOS.
rules.evidence: Baseline

rules.rule: Set -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% on html.
rules.why: It prevents font inflation in landscape.
rules.evidence: Baseline

rules.rule: In the baseline, apply touch-action: manipulation, user-select: none and -webkit-user-select: none to button, a and [role="button"], and keep all :hover rules inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
rules.why: It removes tap delay, long-press selection and sticky hover from the start.
rules.evidence: all :hover rules live here

rules.rule: Run the Never Ship table as a self-check before finishing any mobile work.
rules.why: It lists the defects that must not ship and their replacements.
rules.evidence: Never Ship: Self-check before you finish

rules.rule: Report mobile fixes in a few lines: what was wrong (symptom and one-line why), what changed (file and declaration), and what needs a phone; do not pad it into a report.
rules.why: The code is the deliverable.
rules.evidence: Output

decisions.question: Which height unit should a full-height element use on mobile?

options.name: 100dvh (dynamic)
options.effect: Resizes as the URL bar shows and hides, tracking the visible area; causes layout shifts on marketing content mid-scroll.
options.when: App shells, drawers and anything bottom-pinned.

options.name: 100svh (small)
options.effect: The smallest the viewport gets; stable and never overflows, so nothing is cut off.
options.when: Heroes and first screens on marketing pages.

options.name: 100lvh or 100vh (large)
options.effect: The height with browser chrome collapsed; on load it overflows by the URL bar and bottom-pinned buttons sit under it.
options.when: Almost never; 100vh only as a fallback line for old browsers when the support matrix demands it.

decisions.recommendation: 100dvh for app shells and bottom-pinned UI, 100svh for heroes; never 100vh for an app shell and never 100dvh on a marketing hero.
decisions.evidence: 3. Layout has the wrong height; Never Ship

decisions.question: Should the page itself bounce and pull-to-refresh when scrolled past the top?

options.name: overscroll-behavior: none on html and body
options.effect: No pull-to-refresh on Android Chrome and no whole-page rubber band on iOS; the app feels installed.
options.when: Apps with their own scroll containers, a drawer dragged down, or a canvas.

options.name: Keep default page overscroll
options.effect: Pull-to-refresh and page bounce stay available.
options.when: A scrolling document where pull-to-refresh is welcome.

decisions.recommendation: none on the root for apps, and overscroll-behavior: contain on every inner scrollable; drop the root rule only for scrolling documents.

decisions.question: How should a horizontal carousel handle swipes?

options.name: Native scroll with scroll-snap
options.effect: scroll-snap-type: x mandatory on the track and scroll-snap-align: start on slides; uses the browser's own physics and needs no touch-action.
options.when: When the carousel can be native scroll.

options.name: JS gesture with touch-action: pan-y
options.effect: The carousel handles horizontal drags while the browser keeps vertical panning, stopping the page from jittering.
options.when: When the carousel is a custom JavaScript gesture.

decisions.recommendation: If the carousel is native scroll, use scroll-snap: the browser's own physics beat a hand-rolled spring and touch-action becomes unnecessary; if it is a JS gesture, set touch-action: pan-y.

decisions.question: Which touch-action value should a gesture surface get?

options.name: manipulation
options.effect: No double-tap zoom, so click fires immediately without the 300ms delay.
options.when: Buttons, links, [role=button] and other tappables.

options.name: pan-y
options.effect: Browser keeps vertical panning; the element handles horizontal.
options.when: Horizontal carousels.

options.name: pan-x
options.effect: Browser keeps horizontal panning; the element handles vertical drags.
options.when: Vertical sheet handles.

options.name: none
options.effect: The element handles every axis; the user cannot scroll past it.
options.when: Only custom gestures that own every axis, like a drag-to-dismiss sheet or a slider.

decisions.recommendation: Name only what the browser may still do; use none only where the element truly handles everything.
decisions.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy; 9. Carousel scrolls vertically

decisions.question: What font size should form inputs use when the design wants small input text on desktop?

options.name: 16px everywhere
options.effect: iOS Safari never zooms into inputs.
options.when: Default.

options.name: Smaller on desktop, 16px under @media (pointer: coarse)
options.effect: Desktop keeps smaller input text; touch devices get 16px so focus does not zoom the page.
options.when: When the design calls for smaller text in inputs on desktop.

options.name: Disable zoom with maximum-scale=1 or user-scalable=no
options.effect: Stops the zoom but is an accessibility failure.
options.when: Never.

decisions.recommendation: 16px minimum (1rem at the default root size); scale up only under pointer: coarse if desktop needs smaller text; never disable zoom.
decisions.evidence: 4. Page zooms into the input; Hard Rules 4

decisions.question: How should hover styles be switched off on touch devices?

options.name: Capability media query
options.effect: @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) applies hover only to precise hovering pointers; works for mixed devices.
options.when: Always.

options.name: JavaScript touch detection hook
options.effect: e.g. useIsTouchDevice(); the wrong tool for a one-line CSS job.
options.when: Never.

options.name: User agent or screen width sniffing
options.effect: Guesses at touch and fails on iPads with trackpads, touchscreen laptops and phones with a mouse.
options.when: Never.

decisions.recommendation: Gate every hover rule with @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and give touch users :active feedback.
decisions.evidence: Hard Rules 2-3; 1. Hover state stuck after tap; Operating Posture

decisions.question: When should press feedback fire?

options.name: :active in CSS
options.effect: Responds the instant the finger lands, on every input type.
options.when: Default for all tappables.

options.name: pointerdown in JavaScript
options.effect: Responds on press when script is needed.
options.when: When the feedback needs JavaScript.

options.name: click
options.effect: Responds when the finger leaves, which reads as lag even at 0ms.
options.when: Never as the only press feedback.

decisions.recommendation: :active, or pointerdown if JavaScript is needed, at 100-160ms with ease-out.
decisions.evidence: 5. Tap feels laggy: Feedback on release instead of press

decisions.question: How should the status bar and browser chrome color follow the theme?

options.name: One theme-color meta per prefers-color-scheme
options.effect: Light and dark each get a matching bar.
options.when: When the theme follows the OS setting.

options.name: Update theme-color from JavaScript on toggle
options.effect: The bar follows an in-app theme switch.
options.when: When the app switches theme with a class rather than the OS setting.

options.name: A single theme-color
options.effect: Light mode gets a dark bar or dark mode gets a white one.
options.when: Never.

decisions.recommendation: One tag per scheme, valued at the header background color, not the brand color; update from JavaScript if the theme is class-driven.

decisions.question: Where should mobile fixes be verified before calling them done?

options.name: Chrome device emulation
options.effect: Reproduces none of the mobile bugs; shipping on it ships them all.
options.when: Never as proof.

options.name: Xcode Simulator
options.effect: A step up from emulation but still misses touch feel.
options.when: Not as the final check; the source calls it a step up from emulation, so using it for intermediate checks is [inferred].

options.name: Real hardware
options.effect: Shows sticky hover, tap delay, rubber-banding, safe areas and the keyboard.
options.when: Always before done; ideally a phone a few years old, with the keyboard open, once in landscape.

options.name: Installed PWA on hardware
options.effect: Shows standalone-mode changes to viewport, safe areas and status bar.
options.when: When installation is a target.

decisions.recommendation: Real hardware is the bar; say which fixes still need a device if you cannot test on one.
decisions.evidence: Hard Rules 5; 11. Right in Chrome, wrong on phone

process.detail: Start from the symptom table, match what the user sees, and read that section for the reason and the exact code.

process.step: Apply the fix where its reason holds
process.detail: Use the CSS declaration or meta tag, not JavaScript, and apply it only where the why applies (for example user-select: none on controls, never on body).
Use (hover: hover), (pointer: fine), (pointer: coarse), env() and dvh/svh instead of user agent or width checks.
For a new mobile-facing app, add the viewport and theme-color meta tags and the html, input and button CSS baseline before the first component.

Connect the phone over USB, run the dev server on 0.0.0.0, open by LAN IP, inspect via Safari > Develop or chrome://inspect; use an older phone, open the keyboard, try landscape once, and test as an installed PWA if that is a target.
Check the output against the Never Ship table before finishing.
State what was wrong (symptom and one-line why), what changed (file and declaration), and what needs a phone to confirm; the code is the deliverable.

examples.what: Sticky hover on a button that scales up
examples.visual_note: A button with a hover scale stays scaled up after being tapped, because touch browsers apply :hover on the first tap and leave it; fixed by gating hover behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
A translucent highlight painted over any tapped element with a click handler; the loudest sign that a page is a website.
On load the URL bar is visible, so a 100vh element overflows by its height and a bottom-pinned button sits hidden under it.
Focusing an input under 16px zooms the page and it does not zoom back on blur, leaving a cropped, drifted layout.
.button transitions transform 100ms var(--ease-out) and background 100ms; :active scales to 0.97 and changes background to var(--gray-4), so the button responds as the finger lands.

examples.where: Notch, Dynamic Island and home indicator zones
examples.visual_note: With viewport-fit=cover the page paints edge to edge; the header pads top by env(safe-area-inset-top), the bottom bar pads by env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and a sheet pads by calc(1rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)).
Holding a finger on a web button selects its text or pops the copy/share callout on a link; native controls never do this.
A horizontal swipe makes the page jitter up while the carousel moves because the browser guesses the axis; touch-action: pan-y or native scroll-snap fixes it.
With a single theme-color, light mode gets a dark bar or dark mode a white one; separate tags per scheme (#ffffff light, #0a0a0a dark in the sample) fix it.

examples.where: iPads with trackpads, laptops with touchscreens, phones with a mouse
examples.visual_note: Why touch and mouse must be handled together and gated by capability.

Viewport meta with viewport-fit=cover and interactive-widget=resizes-content, per-scheme theme-color, html tap-highlight transparent, text-size-adjust 100%, overscroll none, 16px inputs, touch-action manipulation and user-select none on buttons and links, and all hover rules in the capability query.
